sentence: This project studies how hardware failures and design bugs affect deep neural networks and builds hardware and algorithm designs that make them more reliable.
This project studies the mathematics of imaging methods that combine ultrasound with electromagnetic waves and develops efficient algorithms for image reconstruction.
This project studies when waves in a plasma travel along protected paths and resist being scattered in realistic plasma conditions.
This project studies how mixtures of charged polymers form microscopic droplets by stretching a single molecule with a magnetic field.
This project studies how fruit fly embryos use the ratio of nuclear content to cytoplasmic volume to time gene activation.
This project builds genetic tools in morning glory plants to find out how changes in DNA shape plant form and responses to environmental change.
This project studies how energy moves through a chain of nonlinear oscillators and builds deep learning tools to solve related equations.
This project builds artificial intelligence methods to design biosensors from two-dimensional materials and studies how model transparency affects what designers learn.
This project develops statistical methods that give valid answers when black-box algorithms are used on complex data, by adapting cross-validation.
This project studies what happens at the point where quantum entanglement is lost in materials made of many interacting electrons.
This project studies how a group of proteins helps plant cells deliver membrane and cell wall material to the plasma membrane.
This project studies why machine learning models with many parameters overfit and builds tools that explain what black-box models are doing.
This project studies how protein nanowires let bacteria move electrons outside the cell and measures how well the nanowires conduct electricity.
This project builds a photoacoustic imaging system that needs just one detector instead of hundreds by tagging sound waves and decoding the signals.
This project studies how semiconductor and metal nanoparticles and the molecules on their surfaces change under intense light and elevated temperature.
This project measures the chemistry of individual foraminifera shells to learn how ocean warming and the carbon cycle changed during a time of rapid climate change.
This project builds computer models of gallium nitride devices to predict how they behave at very low temperatures and to guide circuit design.
This project studies how the chemical lubabegron breaks down in beef cattle, surface waters and soils and tests the toxicity of its products.
